research_question: How do the presence of heat and an acid catalyst influence the product of an esterification reaction?
objective: Produce two esters through esterification and acetylation reactions; qualitatively identify the ester formed in reaction 1; quantitatively determine the experimental yield of acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin) in reaction 2.
hypothesis: If the temperature increases and sulfuric acid is present as a catalyst, then the esterification reaction equilibrium will shift towards ester formation, increasing the amount of product observed.

reactions.name: Esterification (pentyl acetate)
reactions.equation_text: Acetic acid + pentanol -> pentyl acetate + water
qualitative_observations: Two phases observed due to polarity differences.
After heating, clearer phase separation; upper organic layer collected.
After adding saturated NaCl, separation became clearer.
Odor shifted from vinegar/alcohol to sweet fruity banana-like odor (ester).
At 100°C, changes were faster and ester odor dominated.

reactions.name: Acetylation (aspirin synthesis)
reactions.equation_text: Salicylic acid + acetic anhydride -> acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin) + acetic acid
qualitative_observations: Salicylic acid initially a fine white crystalline powder.
After adding acetic anhydride, strong pungent irritating odor; suspension cleared during heating.
After adding cold distilled water, solution turned opaque and white crystals formed.
At 100°C, crystallization occurred more rapidly and crystals were larger/more visible.

core_workflow: Prepare water bath at target temperature.
Combine reagents and add sulfuric acid catalyst under supervision.
safety_actions: Wear goggles, lab coat, and gloves.
Handle concentrated sulfuric acid with instructor assistance.
Dispose acidic/organic waste in designated chemical waste containers.

safety: Concentrated sulfuric acid is highly corrosive.
Acetic anhydride is irritating and produces stinging fumes.
Pentanol and acetic acid are flammable and have irritating fumes.
environment: Reaction residues were collected as chemical waste (not poured down the sink).
ethics: No human participants; no personal data collected.

systematic_errors: Limited precision of volume measurement tools.
Temperature instability due to improvised heating setup.
Incomplete drying can inflate measured mass (yields > 100%).
Impurities/unreacted reagents can remain in products.

conclusion.summary: Heat and catalyst promoted product formation (ester odor and aspirin crystals observed), but yield accuracy was affected by experimental limitations and incomplete drying.
